findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify exactly what ticket text is fed to the ticket_digest prompt for the per-ticket digest (and what the content-hash cache key hashes), and confirm it is fully recoverable from the committed fixture (or widen the fixture to store that input), so candidates 2 and 3 are reproducible.
evidence: Plan: 'LLM digests produced with the retired ticket_digest prompt ... One call per ticket, cached keyed by content hash.'
Plan fixture stores 'titles and the first 2,000 characters of description per ticket'
Epic 62dc comment: digest extracted 'from title + description + every comment'
Acceptance criterion requires measurements 'reproducible from the committed benchmark spec'
findings.finding: The digest-generation input for candidates 2 and 3 is unspecified: the plan says 'One call per ticket' with the retired ticket_digest prompt, but does not state what ticket text is fed to that prompt. The fixture stores only title + first 2,000 chars of description, whereas the original ticket_digest prompt (per epic 62dc's architecture comment) consumed 'title + description + every comment'. Without pinning the digest input, the digest (and thus candidates 2 and 3, and the recorded recall tables) is not reproducible from the committed fixture.
scenarios: Re-running measure.py on another machine produces different digests (and recall numbers) because the digest input differs from what the fixture captured.
A reviewer re-deriving the content-hash cache key cannot reproduce it because the hashed input is undefined.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a covering criterion for evals/similar-tickets/README.md (e.g. it documents the command lines and the stratification rule), or drop it from Scope if not required.
evidence: Scope: 'evals/similar-tickets/README.md (new)'
No AC references the README's content or presence
findings.finding: evals/similar-tickets/README.md is a named deliverable in Scope but no acceptance criterion covers its existence or content.
scenarios: Executor ships without the README or with an empty one and all ACs still pass

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the per-ticket fallback for the ticket_digest sub-step: what measure.py does when a single ticket's digest call fails/errors or validates to empty fields (retry, skip-and-record, or exclude the pair), so one bad call neither aborts the run nor silently skews the per-stratum recall tables.
evidence: Plan: 'Model: the trivial class ... One call per ticket, cached keyed by content hash.' — no per-ticket failure path.

Plan specifies a fallback only at candidate granularity: 'The credentials-absent skip is widened to catch AccessDeniedException, recording candidate 3 unavailable' — nothing for a single digest call among 630 tickets.

TicketDigest fields are all list[str] except component_or_area: a model return with empty propositions/problem_keywords would yield an empty BM25F document and a degenerate embedding paragraph, silently harming recall for that pair's ticket rather than aborting or being recorded.

ABSENCE: over 630 tickets x digest calls, at least one transient failure or empty-field validation is likely; the plan does not say whether such a ticket is retried, skipped, recorded as a hole in the fixture, or excluded from the measured pair set.
findings.finding: The per-ticket ticket_digest LLM call (the shared sub-step feeding candidates 2 and 3) has no specified fallback for a single ticket whose call fails, errors, or returns a structured output that validates to empty fields; only a whole-candidate Bedrock AccessDenied/credentials fallback is specified.
findings.location: Approach — candidate 2 'One call per ticket, cached keyed by content hash' and Digest serialization paragraph
scenarios: A ticket_digest call for one ticket raises a transient/parse error mid-run over the 630-ticket fixture.
The trivial model returns valid JSON with an empty propositions list, producing an empty retrievable document for candidates 2 and 3.
findings.suggested_fix: State that a failed digest call is retried once and, on repeated failure or an all-empty TicketDigest, the ticket is recorded in the fixture header as a digest hole and its pairs are excluded from candidates 2 and 3's recall denominators (not pooled into a silent miss).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify concurrency/ownership for the catch-up update to the shared similar.sqlite index (e.g. a write lock / single-writer transaction / idempotent re-derivation keyed by SHA) so concurrent reader processes cannot corrupt or double-apply the incremental update.
evidence: 'the index location (<repo>/.git/rebar/similar.sqlite ... rebuilt on mismatch), the catch-up rule (reader-process incremental update ...)'
Multiple reader processes are the natural consumer of a shared SQLite index; the plan assigns the update to 'reader-process' but names no concurrency/ownership mechanism
findings.finding: The ADR documents the production index (.git/rebar/similar.sqlite) with a 'reader-process incremental update from git diff' catch-up rule, but does not state how concurrent reader processes are serialized against the same SQLite file. Two reader processes catching up simultaneously on a stale SHA would each attempt to rebuild/update the shared index, with no stated lock/ownership, risking a torn or doubly-applied incremental update.
findings.location: Approach — 'the catch-up rule (reader-process incremental update from git diff --name-only <indexed_sha> <head>)'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile AC2 ('all three candidates') with the Approach's 'candidate 3 may be unavailable' clause — state explicitly whether 'unavailable' is an acceptable terminal state for the ADR or a blocker.
evidence: AC2: 'Recall@5 and recall@10 are recorded per stratum for all three candidates in the ADR'
Approach: 'recording candidate 3 unavailable with the error instead of aborting — and an unavailable candidate may not be selected by the ADR'
findings.finding: Acceptance Criterion 2 demands recall recorded 'for all three candidates' while the Approach permits candidate 3 to be recorded 'unavailable' with no recall numbers — two sections point the implementer in opposite directions on whether all-three numbers are mandatory.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria 2 vs Approach (Auth precondition paragraph)
scenarios: Executor cannot tell whether an 'unavailable' candidate 3 satisfies AC2 or fails it

evidence: 3 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the failure disposition for TRANSIENT Bedrock/model errors (throttle/429, timeout, 5xx) separately from the permanent AccessDenied/credentials-absent case — e.g. retry-with-backoff on retryable errors, and do not record a retryable throttle as permanently 'unavailable'.
evidence: Plan catches only AccessDeniedException and credentials-absent: 'The credentials-absent skip is widened to catch AccessDeniedException, recording candidate 3 unavailable with the error instead of aborting'
630 Titan embedding calls + one Claude call per ticket are made; the plan states no retry/backoff for transient errors
Rebar disposition vocabulary (WAIT_AND_RETRY / retryable vs fatal) applies: a 429 is retryable, AccessDenied is permanent — these must not be collapsed into one 'unavailable' bucket
findings.finding: The plan handles only two external-call failure modes explicitly — credentials-absent and AccessDeniedException (both treated as permanent 'unavailable') — but says nothing about the disposition of TRANSIENT Bedrock/model failures (a ThrottlingException/429, a socket timeout, a 5xx) that can occur across the 630 Titan calls and the per-ticket Claude calls. Without a stated disposition, a transient throttle mid-run could either abort the whole eval (losing cached progress) or be silently recorded as 'unavailable', masking a retryable condition as a permanent one.
findings.location: Approach — 'The credentials-absent skip is widened to catch AccessDeniedException, recording candidate 3 unavailable'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a disposition clause: transient Bedrock errors (ThrottlingException, timeout, 5xx) are retryable and retried with backoff; only AccessDeniedException / credentials-absent are the permanent 'unavailable' disposition that bars ADR selection.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Route a one-call Titan `invoke_model` smoke (under an entitled developer identity) to a SPIKE that confirms the request body `{inputText, dimensions:1024, normalize:true}` and the response's embedding key/shape before committing candidate 3, since this is a new endpoint surface rebar has only ever reached via the Converse API.
evidence: Plan: 'called with the boto3 `bedrock-runtime` client's `invoke_model` and a JSON body of {"inputText": ..., "dimensions": 1024, "normalize": true}'

Existing rebar Bedrock path is Converse via pydantic-ai: bedrock_model.py:101 builds the client, structured.py:59 probes the Converse operation; no invoke_model call exists in src/ (search_files for 'def invoke_model' and 'inputText' returned no repo matches)

iam_s7.tf scopes bedrock:InvokeModel to anthropic.claude-* only (lines 15-18); Titan is unentitled, so the response-parsing contract cannot be exercised in the default environment — this is a NEW endpoint surface on an already-used vendor, Partially-verified (boto3 + invoke_model exist; the Titan V2 surface/response shape is unconfirmed)
The plan states the entitlement resolution (developer identity or add Titan ARN) but names no verification of the invoke_model body/response shape
findings.finding: Candidate 3 is a new endpoint surface (direct boto3 invoke_model against Titan V2) that rebar has never exercised — all existing Bedrock usage is the Converse API via pydantic-ai — and because the id is unentitled in the default environment the invoke_model request/response contract (body keys and the embedding-extraction response shape) cannot be probed there; the plan routes the entitlement gap to a developer identity but does not route a one-call shape smoke to a SPIKE before committing the embedding candidate.
findings.location: Approach, candidate 3 (Titan Text Embeddings V2) and the Auth precondition paragraph
scenarios: The developer runs candidate 3 under an entitled identity but the assumed response key (e.g. body['embedding']) or the 1024-dim/normalize body differs from Titan V2's actual contract, producing a silent parse failure or wrong vectors after the entitlement hurdle is cleared
findings.suggested_fix: Add a pre-plan spike step: make a single real Titan V2 invoke_model call under the entitled developer identity, record the exact response JSON path used to extract the 1024-d vector, and capture it in the fixture header alongside the entitlement check already specified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Require the ADR to reconcile the reintroduced embedding candidate against ADR 0086's recorded rejection of embeddings — citing its prior art (Cupid / arXiv:2308.10022, the ANN->100K-vector threshold) and explicitly weighing the new `bedrock` dependency against 0086's 'Anthropic-only, no-heavy-ML, no-new-dependency' grain — so any reversal is justified rather than silent.
evidence: ADR 0086 Decision #1: 'Cupid digests WITHOUT embeddings (arXiv:2308.10022) ... So the digest — not an embedding — is the load-bearing artifact, keeping rebar on its Anthropic-only, no-heavy-ML grain (no vector DB, no new dependency).'
ADR 0086 Decision #2: 'Brute-force BM25F, not an ANN index ... the unanimous research verdict is that ANN pays off only >100K vectors — we are 100-1000x below that.'
Web-confirmed: arXiv:2308.10022 'CUPID: Leveraging ChatGPT for More Accurate Duplicate Bug Report Detection' is real and directly on-topic (LLM-digest duplicate detection).
Plan Approach candidate 3 adds Titan V2 + 'the bedrock extra's pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]' — a new dependency 0086 avoided by design.
The plan's AC require justifying the choice 'from the semantic stratum' but do not require addressing 0086's recorded no-embeddings/no-new-dependency rationale.
findings.finding: The plan reintroduces an embedding/vector candidate (Amazon Titan V2) and a new `bedrock` extra dependency, but neither the ADR acceptance criteria nor the Approach require the ADR to reconcile with ADR 0086, the direct predecessor that evaluated this same architecture space and explicitly REJECTED embeddings — citing the Cupid digest paper (arXiv:2308.10022), the 'ANN pays off only >100K vectors' research verdict, and a deliberate 'Anthropic-only, no-heavy-ML grain (no vector DB, no new dependency)' posture.
findings.location: Approach (candidate 3) and Acceptance Criteria (3rd bullet: ADR names one architecture and justifies it from the semantic stratum)
scenarios: The new measurement picks vector/Titan as the winner, but the ADR never explains why the earlier recorded decision against embeddings (and its grain/dependency objection) no longer holds, leaving a silent reversal of a documented architectural stance.
A reviewer of the ADR cannot tell whether the embedding candidate's new `bedrock` dependency cost was weighed against 0086's explicit no-new-dependency posture.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Approach and to the ADR-justification acceptance criterion a requirement that the ADR cite ADR 0086 and arXiv:2308.10022, restate 0086's no-embeddings / ANN->100K / no-new-dependency rationale, and state on the re-measured per-stratum evidence why that rationale does or does not still hold before selecting (or rejecting) candidate 3; if candidate 3 is selected, the ADR must account for the added `bedrock` extra dependency cost.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion that candidate 3 produces real per-stratum recall numbers from a successful live Titan call (under the developer entitlement or after adding the Titan ARN), so the semantic-stratum decision is never made on an 'unavailable' candidate.
evidence: 'The credentials-absent skip is widened to catch AccessDeniedException, recording candidate 3 unavailable with the error instead of aborting'
AC2: 'Recall@5 and recall@10 are recorded per stratum for all three candidates'
AC3 justifies the architecture 'from the semantic stratum' — the stratum where vector is the key contender
epic rationale: decision must rest on measurement, not an unmeasured proxy (the July N=8 complaint)
findings.finding: No acceptance criterion requires a successful live Titan embedding call producing real vectors; the plan explicitly permits recording candidate 3 as 'unavailable' on AccessDeniedException, so the decisive vector candidate can be bypassed and the ADR's architecture chosen without the risky new path ever executing against live Bedrock.
scenarios: Executor runs in the default (unentitled) environment, candidate 3 returns unavailable, and the ADR is written from only fts5 + digest numbers — repeating the epic's unmeasured-decision failure
findings.suggested_fix: Add AC: 'measure.py --candidate vector completes a live amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0 call and records non-empty recall@5/@10 for both strata; the fixture header records the entitled identity and its passing entitlement check. An unavailable candidate 3 blocks ADR completion.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a known-answer correctness test for the recall@k computation (a small constructed candidate ranking whose expected recall@5/@10 per stratum is known) so a metric bug cannot silently produce the ADR's decision tables.
evidence: Happy-path test only asserts a table prints and pairs resolve to existing ids — not that the recall number is correct
The recall figures are the decision criterion ('justifies it from the semantic stratum'), so their correctness is load-bearing
findings.finding: The core new logic of this story is the recall@5/@10 computation per stratum — the numbers that drive the ADR's architecture decision — yet the testing plan validates only that a table prints and that pairs resolve. No test exercises the recall metric against a known-answer case (a constructed ranking where the expected recall@k is known), so an off-by-one or mis-stratified recall bug would silently produce wrong tables that are then copied verbatim into the ADR.
findings.location: Testing — 'prints a per-stratum recall table; the fixture loads and every pair resolves'
